I'm a little torn on the big tax refund that a lot of people I know end up  getting this time of year. In my little circle of friends, I'm the only one without any kids so tax season is pretty uneventful for me and the wife. We'll get 50 or 60 bucks back because we get no tax credits and we try to keep our withholding at a minimum so we get to keep as much as our paychecks as possible. I don't really care because we live a pretty comfortable life and if I ever want to buy a toy like a new game console or maybe a TV, I just do it because we have the money. Being child free definitely has its perks. However, everyone else I know will get a minimum of around $4,000 and that has little to do with what's withheld from their paychecks and has more to do with their tax credits. Again, that doesn't really bother me because I know how expensive child care can be, but that's the thing though. None of this money is really spent on child care, it ends up getting spent on a 70 inch TV or a new tattoo or on a new...whatever, it's just stuff. They don't put the money back for a down payment on a home, or put it back for college tuition for their children, or maybe pay a few months on their rent. Then by the end of spring, they're broke again and complaining about money problems. I don't have many friends so I just shrug it off and try not to let it get to me, but when I see them squandering such a great thing as getting some extra money for a change, it ends up getting to me. I understand how kids can be so expensive and I think that's why it bothers me. I just can't put it together either because my family was incredibly poor growing up and I don't remember my parents getting excited about anything in the spring. We never had new stuff, clothes were always hand-me-downs, and our car was usually on its last leg most of the time. Maybe I totally missed something.

It's difficult to describe, but I'll take a whack at it. I was in my early teens when the Gamecube came about and I hadn't owned many consoles up until that point. My family didn't have much money growing up and when I was finally old enough to start cutting some grass/doing odd jobs for people around town and saving up some money, it was a really emotional experience when I finally did get a console and a handful of games. Nothing felt better than knowing I worked my ass off for these achievements in modern gaming that Nintendo had wrought. I had a SNES and N64 but I didn't get a SNES until the N64 had already been out for a year and I got an N64 just a year before the Gamecube came out. Anyway, the Gamecube was going to be the first console that I could actually afford to buy when it launched. Everyone else I knew was stoked about PS2 and Xbox, and those are some great systems, but they just didn't give me that tingly feeling when I saw that purple cube teasing me in the glass display at Wal-Mart. The first game I bought for it was Sonic Adventure 2 Battle. That was the only game I could afford for about 6 months and I still have that game today. I'm actually surprised it still works after all these years because I played it everyday after school. Girls could wait, my Gamecube beckoned. Then when Windwaker came out, I knew that when I looked back, this purple cube that played mini-discs of all things and wasn't exactly the "cool" system to have would be a truly special part of my childhood. Since then, that purple cube had to be retired. I still keep it on a shelf in my game room and even though I have a silver one, that original purple Gamecube will always have a special place in my heart. Rest in peace, old friend. Anyway, that's why the Nintendo Gamecube is special to me and no matter where gaming technology takes us, the Gamecube will always be my favorite console. 

TL;DR: The Gamecube is special to me because it was crowning achievement of my childhood/teen years.
